players.analysis: Singleton, a former five-star recruit, has been a disappointment over his four-year career at Penn State. His final rushing line this past year was 123-549-13, mainly profiling as a red zone runner. Singleton would likely have dominated at the NFL Combine, but he suffered a broken bone in his foot at the Senior Bowl. He may not produce much in 2026 in a crowded Titans backfield, but Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears are set to become free agents after this season.

players.name: Jacoby Brissett
players.analysis: Brissett isn't a long-term solution, but his play down the stretch in 2025 could get him a starting opportunity to open 2026. The veteran turned 33 in December.

players.name: MarShawn Lloyd
players.analysis: Lloyd’s college career began at South Carolina with a 2020 ACL tear. A quiet two-year stretch followed – then a move to USC. In 2023, he handled a 1A role alongside fifth-year senior Austin Jones (116 carries to 85). Lloyd displayed plus vision, acceleration, and open-field elusiveness en route to 7.1 yards per carry. Injuries ruined his 2024 and 2025 seasons, but there's some sleeper appeal here if Lloyd can swat the injury bug.

players.name: Jalen McMillan
players.analysis: McMillan missed most of 2025 with a neck injury, but he returned late to post 7-114-0 against the Dolphins. His short-term outlook improved significantly after Mike Evans signed a multi-year deal in San Francisco.

players.name: Pat Freiermuth
players.analysis: Freiermuth had an uneven year in 2025 while sharing snaps and targets with Darnell Washington and Jonnu Smith. Freiermuth ended with 38-435-4, good for TE26 in fantasy points per game. There's some hope for a bounce back, as Jonnu Smith left via free agency. Pittsburgh's pass volume should also tick up under new HC Mike McCarthy.

players.name: Rachaad White
players.analysis: We were pumped to see White — an athletic back with pass-catching ability — land in Round 3 in 2022. He managed to get on the field early and eventually work in tandem with Leonard Fournette. 2023 turned up workhorse usage, boosted by a thin backfield and a surprisingly effective Baker Mayfield. However, we baked in some dynasty risk following the 2024 arrival of Bucky Irving, who proved pro-ready. White was largely quiet in 2025 -- despite some missed time from Irving. Washington supplies a nice landing spot, but the team could add more talent via the draft.

players.name: Hunter Henry
players.analysis: Henry went 55-712-7 during the 2025 fantasy season, living on his ability to score TDs. He turns 32 during a contract season in 2026 but remains a short-term streamer.

players.name: Kyle Williams
players.analysis: Williams did very little in his rookie season, but there were flashes of being a great deep target. Williams went 10-209-3 in 2025 and should earn a larger role in 2026. But, the Patriots will likely address the position further with young WRs to compete with Williams.

players.name: Terrance Ferguson
players.analysis: Ferguson showed a late-season surge with Davante Adams sidelined. The Rams seem intent on using the young TE as a pseudo WR, which is great for his fantasy potential. Still, uncertainty at QB and a crowded TE depth chart mean dynasty managers will need patience.

players.name: Nathaniel Dell
players.analysis: Between his leg fracture in 2023 and dislocated kneecap and torn ACL in 2024, Dell did not play at all in 2025. His career is in jeopardy, but if Dell can somehow get back healthy, he could be a sneaky add on deep dynasty rosters.

players.name: Juwan Johnson
players.analysis: Johnson had a career year in 2025, posting 74-828-3 on 97 targets during the fantasy season. With Shough showing promise as the starter, Johnson should retain streaming value in the short term. We're not concerned with the arrival of Noah Fant via free agency.

players.name: Eli Stowers
players.analysis: Stowers is a former QB converted to TE. He will be more slot WR than TE, sitting at 6'4, 235 pounds. He led Vanderbilt with 62 catches last year and was a reliable option for QB Diego Pavia. Stowers has elite explosiveness and short-area quickness, and that was reflected in his excellent Combine performance. Stowers will be the future starting TE for the Eagles. Dallas Goedert is set to be a free agent after this season.

players.name: Skyler Bell
players.analysis: Bell transferred to UConn in 2024 and broke out. Over the past two seasons, he caught 151-2138-18. He isn't built like an NFL WR, but the production is hard to ignore with Bell able to beat man coverage. He lands in a great situation with Josh Allen as a potential No. 3 WR on the Bills.

players.name: Jack Bech
players.analysis: Bech disappointed as a rookie, especially considering the poor WR depth chart for the Raiders. He went 20-224-0 in 2025 and will be paired with a. new coaching staff in 2026. Perhaps Bech can still develop and earn the slot job next season with a rookie QB, so he is worth stashing.

players.name: Mark Andrews
players.analysis: Andrews signed a three-year extension with the Ravens during the 2025 season, locking him into the team for the foreseeable future. With Isaiah Likely out of town, Andrews should be able to gain TE1 value in the short term. Note that 2026 will be his age-31 season.

players.name: Deshaun Watson
players.analysis: Watson sustained an Achilles tear in Week 7 of the 2024 season. There’s a chance he doesn’t start another NFL game, although he remains under contract with the Browns.

players.name: Jake Ferguson
players.analysis: The Cowboys offensive resurgence translated to production from Ferguson. He went 81-595-8 on 100 targets during the fantasy season. He didn't display any amazing athletic skills, but Ferguson's soft hands and good route running made him a reliable option for Dak Prescott. Ferguson signed a four-year extension and is locked in with the Cowboys long term.

players.name: Tyler Allgeier
players.analysis: Allgeier has proven effective as an early-down thumper, but Bijan Robinson capped the fantasy ceiling in Atlanta. While he’s out of Bijan’s shadow in Arizona, the Cardinals will place him in a similar situation after spending the third overall pick on Jeremiyah Love. Allgeier now projects as more of a handcuff than a standalone fantasy option.

players.name: Eli Raridon
players.analysis: Raridon stands to be a two-way TE at the next level with solid blocking skills showing development as a pass catcher as well.  Hunter Henry is getting older and Raridon's Day 2 draft capital could make him the heir apparent. He offers intriguing upside if you can stash him for a bit.

players.name: Malik Benson
players.analysis: Benson is a speed demon who never quite broke out after his JUCO stint. After flopping at Alabama, Benson took the Evan Stewart deep role at Oregon this past season. Benson offers another deep threat for the Raiders behind Tre Tucker and Dont'e Thornton.

players.name: Dalton Schultz
players.analysis: Schultz had one of his best years in 2026, going 78-704-3 during the fantasy season. He posted the most targets of his career at 106. Schultz is locked into the Texans and QB C.J. Stroud for one more season. He should be a suitable low-end TE1 for 2026, but the future is cloudy beyond that.

players.name: Chigoziem Okonkwo
players.analysis: Okonkwo posted five top-12 fantasy finishes in 2025, his final year in Tennessee. He set career highs in targets (79), catches (56) and yards (560) but remained an underwhelming TD producer (2). He also played all 17 games for the fourth straight season. In Washington, he'll have a chance to boost production for an offense that's moving on from Zach Ertz.

players.name: Tank Bigsby
players.analysis: Bigsby wrapped up a productive career at Auburn with 540-2,903-25 (35 games). He tested as an average athlete at the Combine, however, and his struggles carried over into a mistake-filled first season. Bigsby looked like a different back in 2024, showing the power and burst that made him an attractive prospect. A wrench was thrown into his 2025 plans, as the Jags traded him to Philly over the summer. He’ll remain in a backup/handcuff role.

players.name: Jerry Jeudy
players.analysis: Jeudy struggled to make an impact amidst the terrible Browns' QBs in 2025. He went 50-602-2 in 2025 and didn't look particularly sharp. A new offense (and potentially QB) could help Jeudy get back to contributing for fantasy teams, but the days of him being a top dynasty option are over.

players.name: Travis Kelce
players.analysis: With the Chiefs' offense taking a step back in 2005, Kelce felt the sting. He finished with 73-839-5 on his fantasy season, his lowest reception total since 2015. In March, we learned that he'd return for his 14th season in Kansas City. He's now year-to-year, making him a shaky dynasty asset.

players.name: Dallas Goedert
players.analysis: Goedert had a TD-heavy 2025 going 60-591-11. The Eagles schemed up red zone touches for him to score as much as he did, but that may not happen in the future. Goedert is set to be a free agent in 2026, but he is unlikely to find a better situation than the Eagles. He will be 31 heading into the 2026 season and may have peaked in terms of his fantasy output.

players.name: Marvin Mims Jr.
players.analysis: Mims Jr. fell behind Troy Franklin and Pat Bryan in the WR pecking order. He went 37-322-1, but Mims is still an elite returner who will stick on the roster. He just won't have the fantasy impact that was promised when he was drafted.

players.name: Keaton Mitchell
players.analysis: Mitchell showed dynamic traits before a December 2023 ACL tear. He missed most of the 2024 season but returned to see part-time work behind Derrick Henry in '25. The results still weren't great: 341 yards and 1 TD on 59 attempts, plus 9 catches for 63 yards. He projects as a part-timer after signing with the Chargers.

players.name: Kimani Vidal
players.analysis: Vidal is short but stout at 5’8, 215 pounds. He posted eye-popping production at Troy that includes 2,793 rushing yards and 24 TDs over his final two seasons. After a quiet 2024, injuries to Najee Harris and Omarion Hampton opened the door for Vidal to post five games of 100+ yards. He'll slide back to a reserve role in '26.

players.name: T.J. Hockenson
players.analysis: Hockenson's best days are behind him as he heads into his age-29 season. The Vikings at least added talent at QB, signing Kyler Murray after enduring a brutal 2025 under J.J. McCarthy.

players.name: Oronde Gadsden II
players.analysis: Gadsden flashed elite fantasy potential early in the season, but it ended with a whimper. Overall, his 47-641-3 stat line is solid for a Round 5 pick who wasn't even active until late September. Los Angeles added TE Charlie Kolar in free agency, but he's expected to be a main contributor in the run game.

players.name: AJ Barner
players.analysis: Barner played ahead of rookie Elijah Arroyo in 2025, but the young athlete may pass Barner sooner rather than later. Barner, only 24, should still remain on dynasty rosters while this situation plays out under new OC Brian Fleury.

players.name: David Montgomery
players.analysis: Montgomery's rushing yardage (716), TD output (8), and catch total (24) regressed in 2025. This, despite appearing in 17 games for the first time in his career. Ultimately, Montgomery's best fantasy days are behind him. He's signed through 2027.

players.name: Jalen Nailor
players.analysis: Nailor continued flashing in 2025 especially in the red zone. He could be a starter for the Raiders with their lack of WR depth

players.name: Brenen Thompson
players.analysis: Thompson played at Oklahoma and Texas early in his career, but barely saw the field. He made the jump to Mississippi State in 2025 and produced, going 57-1054-6 on the season. Thompson is a big play threat who could challenge to be the fastest WR at the NFL Combine this year. Thompson is pretty blocked on the Chargers depth chart, but he may provide an occasional deep threat.

players.name: Jalen Royals
players.analysis: Royals did very little in his rookie year even with Rashee Rice missing most of the season. He only caught two passes in 2025, but could develop into a bigger role in 2026 if other WRs move on from the Chiefs. He is worth hanging onto in case there is offseason buzz.

players.name: Carson Beck
players.analysis: Beck's strong end of the season in the college football playoff propped him up to being drafted in the third round. But Beck was volatile throughout the season. Beck has a ton of experience, and strong footwork makes him an ideal backup QB in the NFL. He will get an opportunity to prove himself at some point this season, but Beck is unlikely to stick as the Cardinals long term franchise QB.

players.name: Seth McGowan
players.analysis: McGowan started at Oklahoma but was charged with robbery and battery on a drug-related crime. He transferred to New Mexico State and succeeded as their starter. Finally, he ended in Kentucky this past year, rushing for 165-725-12. McGowan fell to the seventh round, but appears set to back up Jonathan Taylor

players.name: Anthony Richardson
players.analysis: Richardson lost a camp competition to Daniel Jones in 2025. Then, when Jones suffered an Achilles tear, Richardson wasn't able to play due to a freak eye injury. He requested a trade in April.

players.name: Kevin Coleman Jr.
players.analysis: Coleman was a four-star recruit who started with Deion Sanders at Jackson State. Instead of following Sanders to Colorado, Coleman went to Louisville, but struggled to make an impact. Then he went to Missouri. 2024 was Coleman's best season at Missouri going 74-932-6. Coleman will likely back-up Malik Washington as the slot WR for the Dolphins.

players.name: Demond Claiborne
players.analysis: Claiborne injured his ribs in the first game of the year that seemed to affect him throughout the season. He is a smaller runner with 4.3 speed who can break long runs. He has 21 rushing TDs over the last two years on a weak Wake Forest offense. Claiborne could certainly make the Vikings roster as the third RB and make an impact in 2027.

players.name: Geno Smith
players.analysis: Smith was a major fantasy flop in 2025, posting only two top-12 fantasy finishes. At 35, his days as an NFL starter are nearing an end. But he'll at least have a shot at starting games in 2026 after the Jets acquired him in a trade from Vegas.

players.name: Dylan Sampson
players.analysis: Sampson is a bit light in the pants, but he moves so fluidly, making him tough to bring down. He had six straight 100+ yard rushing games in his final season for Tennessee. Being paired on the Browns with RB Quinshon Judkins makes Samspon an intriguing third-down and pass-catching back moving forward. Sampson caught 33 of 40 targets as a rookie.

players.name: Gunnar Helm
players.analysis: Helm flashed at times during his rookie season, though he still sat behind Chig Okonkwo for most of the year. With Okonkwo leaving in free agency, Helm looked to be in a nice spot for spot-start fantasy value in 2026. That still may be the case, but Tennessee added former Giants TE Daniel Bellinger in free agency on a three-year deal with $14 million guaranteed.

players.name: Aaron Rodgers
players.analysis: Rodgers exceeded expectations in 2025 with 3,322 yards, 24 TDs, and 7 INTs. Still, it's unknown whether he'll return for one more season in 2026. If so, it'll almost certainly be with Pittsburgh and new HC Mike McCarthy.

players.name: Cade Otton
players.analysis: Otton finished at TE29 in PPR points per game last season. The team showed they valued him with a new three-year deal worth $20 million guaranteed, but that doesn't bolster his fantasy prospects. The 27-year-old remains a low-ceiling dynasty asset.

players.name: Shedeur Sanders
players.analysis: Sanders generally underwhelmed across seven late-season starts. The rookie notched a 56.6% completion rate, 6.6 yards per attempt, and a 19.0 QBR. He recorded only one QB1 fantasy finish. Of course, Sanders wasn't surrounded by top talent. Now, we'll see how he's judged by a new coaching staff.

players.name: Adam Randall
players.analysis: Randall came to Clemson as a WR, but transitioned to RB before 2025. The 6'2, 235 back was a track star in high school, so his size and speed offers a unique runner who succeeded on a weak Clemson offense. Randall could fill the Keaton Mitchell role down the line as a change of pace receiving back.

players.name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
players.analysis: Tracy delivered instant value as a rookie with 1,123 total yards, despite New York providing a terrible supporting cast. The arrow was pointing straight up... until the Giants used a Round 4 pick on bruising RB Cam Skattebo. A season-ending injury to Skattebo allowed Tracy to see more work in '25, but the pair figures to work in a timeshare in 2026.

players.name: Keenan Allen
players.analysis: Allen returned to the Chargers and had a strong early season. He ended up going 81-777-4 in 2025, but will turn 34 in the offseason. Allen may have one year left in his NFL career, but will likely have to take a back-up role. It is unlikely he sticks as a fantasy starter in 2026, and certainly is nearing retirement.

players.name: Dohnte Meyers
players.analysis: Meyers showed promise with a 7-82 Week 4 line vs. the Jags. He could stick as Cincy's long-term No. 3 WR.

players.name: Sean Tucker
players.analysis: As a rookie, Tucker watched Rachaad White eventually earn a workhorse role. Then in 2024, he witnessed the breakout of Bucky Irving. Outside of one game vs. Buffalo, Tucker remained quiet in 2025. He returned to Tampa Bay in March, but the signing of Kenneth Gainwell ruins any shot at '26 value.

players.name: Chimere Dike
players.analysis: Dike was a stud returner for the Titans as a rookie in 2025, but he also contributed as a WR. He went 48-423-4 and become the pseudo No. 1 WR on the team. That certainly won't be Dike's role going forward, but he proved he can be a weapon that gets some playing time.

players.name: Brandon Aiyuk
players.analysis: Aiyuk didn't play in 2025 after an ACL, MCL, and meniscus injury in 2024. The 49ers and Aiyuk may sever ties heading into 2026, and he should be fully healthy on a new squad. Aiyuk already disappointed in 2024 before the injury and is heading into his age-28 season. It appears unlikely he turns into a top-12 fantasy WR again.

players.name: Jauan Jennings
players.analysis: Jennings seized the opportunity with Brandon Aiyuk out all of last season and Ricky Pearsall dealing with injuries. The veteran finished as the WR34 in PPR points per game. We'll see where he ends up in free agency.

players.name: Kendre Miller
players.analysis: Durability remained an issue here in 2025. Miller's now totaled only 127 carries through three seasons. 2026 turns up a contract year.

players.name: Alvin Kamara
players.analysis: Kamara set a career low in rushing yards in 2023 (694). He signed a two-year contract extension in October 2024, keeping him under team control through the 2026 season. In '24, he generally outperformed expectations before a late-season groin injury. Another injury surfaced in 2025 -- an MCL sprain -- forcing multiple absences. Now with Travis Etienne in town, Kamara's likely to play elsewhere in the fall.

players.name: Jordan Watkins
players.analysis: Watkins dealt with a high ankle sprain in 2026 and would have had some opportunity to crack the 49ers lineup. He is in a crowded situation going forward.

players.name: Jordan Whittington
players.analysis: Whittington got some play in 2025, but he was still pretty buried on the depth chart with Davante Adams and the TEs emerging. He could have a long NFL career, but it is doubtful Whittington does enough to make a fantasy impact.

players.name: Jaylin Lane
players.analysis: Lane mostly played on special teams for the Commanders, but his speed was utilized on offense at times. He has some upside if he develops, but Lane likely sits toward the end of the depth chart.

players.name: Emanuel Wilson
players.analysis: Wilson saw a surprising 103 carries in 2024, posting 4.9 YPC. His workload rose in '25, largely because of missed games from Josh Jacobs. Wilson hit the spring as a free agent and signed with a Seahawks team that just lost Kenneth Walker to the Chiefs. Zach Charbonnet is also coming off a January ACL tear. Then came the NFL Draft, when serious competition arrived in Round 1 pick Jadarian Price. The rookie puts a major dent into Wilson's dynasty value.

players.name: Jaylen Wright
players.analysis: Wright was one of the speediest RBs in the 2024 class. According to The Athletic’s Bruce Feldman, Wright hit a Tyreek Hill-like 23.6 MPH in practice. The three-year Volunteer averaged a ridiculous 7.4 yards per carry in 2023, with 19 of his 136 attempts going for 15+ yards (per PFF). He showed out at the Combine with a 4.38 forty time and a 38-inch vertical. Miami provided an ideal landing spot for creative usage, but 2024 turned up light work behind De'Von Achane. The same trend surfaced in '25, while Miami also added rookie RB Ollie Gordon. We'll see how this backfield depth shakes out under a new coaching staff.

players.name: Ray Davis
players.analysis: Davis tallied back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons -- one at Vanderbilt and one at Kentucky (2023). 2023 turned up his best work yet, including 3.81 yards after contact per attempt and a career-long 75-yarder on a sizable 73% carry share. After a promising rookie year, Davis' workload regressed in 2025, with 34% of his touches coming in a meaningless Week 18 game. He'll remain far behind James Cook in 2026.

players.name: Max Klare
players.analysis: Klare broke out at Purdue in 2024 with 51-685-4. He took a step back on the Buckeyes last year at 43-448-2, but he showed improved blocking and good route running to be a shallow target. He did have some drops and mental lapses, but Klare can be a Jake Ferguson-type TE. He will split time with Terrance Ferguson, but the rest of the Rams TEs are set to become FAs within the next two years.

players.name: Greg Dulcich
players.analysis: After a bit of a 2025 revival (26-335-1 in nine games), Dulcich signed a fresh one-year deal in Miami. The Fins figure to roll out a low-volume passing game, but Dulcich could be a starting TE, depending on their other offseason additions.

players.name: Xavier Legette
players.analysis: Legette had a disappointing sophomore season going 35-363-3. He was beaten out by rookie Tetairoa McMillan and played more of a reserve role this season. With the Panthers' struggles in the passing game, there is little upside for Legette moving forward, except for him only being 25 years old.

players.name: Oscar Delp
players.analysis: Delp is an H-Back who continues in the line of great Georgia TEs. He went 20-261-1 and was used as a lead blocker often throughout the season. That blocking may get him drafted higher than his production indicates, but Delp's soft hands could be enough to become a better pro than college player. Delp could develop into the starting TE for the Saints. The team has a potential out for Juwan Johnson after this year.

players.name: Joshua Palmer
players.analysis: Palmer signed a sizable deal with the Bills, but he only went 22-303-0 in 2025. Palmer's role is unlikely to grow in the future as the Bills should add more WRs in the offseason.

players.name: Elijah Arroyo
players.analysis: Arroyo had a few flashes in his rookie season, but he was never able to rise past A.J. Barner on the depth chart. Arroyo finished the season at 15-179-1, missing the last few games with a knee injury. Still, at only 23, his athletic upside makes him a dynasty hold.

players.name: Tahj Brooks
players.analysis: Two straight 1,500-yard rushing seasons with double-digit TDs show Brooks’ success at Texas Tech. His shifty feet lead to very few hard hits, and Brooks can certainly hit the home run. Outside of missing one game in 2024 with an arm injury, Brooks has been healthy despite being a bellcow with 576 carries over the past two seasons. He didn't play much as a rookie but could compete for the RB2 role in 2026.

players.name: Evan Engram
players.analysis: Engram had high hopes for 2025, but he fell short of expectations (50-461-1). He now heads into his age-32 season in an offense that's suddenly stacked at WR. We're not banking on a 2026 rebound here.

players.name: Justice Hill
players.analysis: Lightly used on the ground in 2024, Hill still managed to set a career-high with 42 catches. Injuries limited Hill to only 18 carries and 21 catches in 2025. He remains a low-upside dynasty asset.

players.name: Theo Johnson
players.analysis: Johnson was a surprise in 2025, scoring 5 TDs in his first 9 games of the season. He eventually cooled off, hurt by missed time from Jaxson Dart. But the real issue here is the arrival of TE Isaiah Likely, who joins new HC John Harbaugh from Baltimore. While Johnson remains intriguing from an athleticism perspective, his short-term target outlook takes a hit.

players.name: Mike Gesicki
players.analysis: Gesicki returned as the Bengals' starting TE in 2025, but an injury to Joe Burrow and a step back for the offense made him unstartable for most of the year. With the bevy of weapons on the Bengals, Gesicki will remain a spot-starter in the short term.

players.name: Tez Johnson
players.analysis: Johnson stepped up when injuries ravaged the Buccaneers' WRs in 2025. He finished his rookie season going 28-322-5. The depth chart may not give Johnson an opportunity to play a lot moving forward, but his talent makes him rosterable in most dynasty league formats.

players.name: Jordan James
players.analysis: James is a young and explosive runner who is an ideal zone scheme fit. He posted 1,267 rushing yards in his final Oregon season in a split backfield and then went in Round 5 of the 2025 draft. He didn't see a single touch as a rookie, though. There's only an outside chance he's San Francisco's RB2 in 2026.

players.name: Deion Burks
players.analysis: Burks flashed speed and athleticism at Purdue before transferring to Oklahoma, but he was never able to break out. He went 57-620-4 in 2025 after an injury-riddled 2024. Burks sits as a pure slot WR at 5'9, 188 pounds. Burks had a drastic NFL Draft fall to the 7th round and is unlikely to make a major fantasy impact.

players.name: LeQuint Allen
players.analysis: Allen had his background looked into deeply by the NFL after having an assault charge dismissed and expunged from his record. With that aside, he exited college with two straight 1,000-yard rushing seasons and 102 receptions over that period. His multi-faceted skill set makes him a dynasty sleeper, even after a quiet rookie season.

players.name: Colby Parkinson
players.analysis: In 2025, Parkinson had a strong second half as a red zone target for Matthew Stafford. But the TE will be in a crowded situation next season as he competes with Terrance Ferguson for playing time. Parkinson is under contract for one more season.

players.name: Treylon Burks
players.analysis: Burks flashed in a late-season sample with the Commanders. He hit free agency in the spring but re-signed to compete for snaps in a wide-open depth chart.

players.name: Mason Taylor
players.analysis: Taylor saw playing time in his rookie season as the de facto starter for the Jets, although he only mustered 44-369-1. Neck and ankle injuries caused miss games during the season, but his playing time stayed high. While Geno Smith arrived to improve the QB spot, this passing game still profiles as a bottom-five unit.

players.name: Savion Williams
players.analysis: Williams flashed a bit as a rookie, but he remained a unique weapon used in the screen game and trick plays. Williams will have trouble cracking a deep Packers' WR group, but he could find more playing time in 2026.

players.name: Corey Kiner
players.analysis: Kiner looks like New England's No. 3 RB, but that role has generated some early-season opportunities. He's worth a stash in deeper formats.

players.name: KeAndre Lambert-Smith
players.analysis: Lambert-Smith had preseason hype coming into his rookie season, but it didn't really pay off. He went 5-51-1 as a rookie, but should land on the team next year and may develop more.

players.name: Darnell Mooney
players.analysis: Mooney took a step back in 2025 going 32-443-1 following up his nearly 1,000 yard season in 2024. Mooney battled injuries throughout the season, but he clearly lost a step in his age-28 season. The Falcons may address the WR position this offseason pushing Mooney further down the depth chart.

players.name: Will Shipley
players.analysis: In 2025, Shipley played a minor role behind Saquon Barkley, who didn't miss a game due to injury. Barkley and Tank Bigsby remain under contract for '26, limiting Shipley's dynasty appeal.

players.name: Konata Mumpfield
players.analysis: Mumpfield saw more snaps late in the season and flashed enough ability to potentially make the Rams in 2026. He is intriguing in very deep leagues on the back end of your dynasty roster.

players.name: Colbie Young
players.analysis: Young was the deep threat for Georgia this year with 26-358-1. He was second on the team in receiving yards behind Zachariah Branch and was built to take the top off of the defense. He could become the No. 4 WR for the Bengals.

players.name: Eli Heidenreich
players.analysis: Heidenreich played the slot back in Navy's option offense, playing in the slot but also taking part in the triple option. That led to going 77-499-3 as a runner and 51-941-6 as a receiver in 2025. He even threw a pass this season. Heidenreich's role on the Steelers remains to be seen, but he may struggle to crack the 53-man roster.

players.name: Devin Singletary
players.analysis: In March of 2024, Singletary inked a three-year, $16.5 million deal with New York. But a poor offensive environment and the rise of Tyrone Tracy Jr. kept Singletary's fantasy production in check that season. The Giants added Cam Skattebo in the '25 draft, although his season-ending injury allowed Singletary to enter a timeshare with Tracy. With Skattebo coming back, Singletary won't be a lock for the 2026 roster.

players.name: Sione Vaki
players.analysis: Vaki brings some intrigue as the direct backup to Jahmyr Gibbs, but there's no standalone value here.

players.name: CJ Daniels
players.analysis: Daniels started at Liberty before transferring to LSU and finally Miami. He was a central cog in the Hurricane's passing game this year to help support QB Carson Beck. Daniels will likely be blocked from moving up the Rams depth chart.

players.name: Jalen Milroe
players.analysis: Milroe exited college with one of the best QB rushing profiles since Lamar Jackson. He'll be developed as a passer behind Sam Darnold, who excelled as the 2025 starter. If this staff can figure out how to harness Milroe’s passing, he could be gangbusters for fantasy in a few years.

players.name: Calvin Ridley
players.analysis: Ridley had a disappointing 2025 going 17-303-0. He will likely move on to a new team, but he recently turned 31. Ridley's best days are behind him, but he could be useful in fantasy if he lands in a pass heavy system with a good QB.

players.name: Marlin Klein
players.analysis: Klein replaced Colston Loveland at Michigan but dealt with nagging injuries over the course of the season. He is another elite athlete who showcases good blocking and soft hands. Klein will need development, but his Day 2 draft capital could make him the future starter at TE for the Texans. He is worth stashing long term if you have space.

players.name: Cooper Kupp
players.analysis: Kupp is nearing the end of his career as he approaches his age-33 season. He took a backseat to JSN going 47-593-2 in 2025. Kupp may have a year or two left, but he won't be startable in fantasy.

players.name: Roschon Johnson
players.analysis: Kyle Monangai's turf toe could open the door for increased playing time in 2026. Still, Johnson offers little to get excited about from a talent standpoint, making him unlikely to carry meaningful dynasty value into 2027.

players.name: James Conner
players.analysis: Despite the addition of rookie Trey Benson, Conner remained the clear starter in 2024. Arizona even signed the veteran to an extension in November of '24, although we'd see his momentum hit a wall in 2025. A September ankle injury cost him the rest of the season and required surgery. We'd bet against a rebound in 2026, especially with the Cardinals adding elite prospect Jeremiyah Love.

players.name: Kaleb Johnson
players.analysis: Johnson's rookie year proved disastrous. After arriving in Round 3, the Iowa standout spread only 28 carries (for 69 yards) across 10 games. He simply wasn't able to earn a role alongside Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell. We then saw how little the team believes in Johnson, as Rico Dowdle arrived on a two-year deal. Note that Warren is signed through the 2027 season.

players.name: Charlie Kolar
players.analysis: Kolar was a productive, multi-year starter at Iowa State. But he played behind Isaiah Likely and Mark Andrews for four seasons in Baltimore, catching only 30 passes. He signed a three-year deal with the Chargers in free agency, one that includes $17 million in guaranteed money. Still, he figures to contribute heavily in the blocking game for OC Mike McDaniel.

players.name: David Njoku
players.analysis: Njoku split time early in the season with rookie Harold Fannin Jr., but the writing was on the wall in the final year of his contract. Njoku eventually slotted behind Fannin and finished the season with 33-293-4. He enters his age-30 season looking for a new team.

players.name: Jahan Dotson
players.analysis: Dotson went 18-262-1 on the Eagles in 2025 and still isn't making a fantasy impact. We are unlikely to see him emerge in 2026.

players.name: Sam Roush
players.analysis: Roush has improved every season, topping out at 49-545-2 in 2025 for Stanford. At 6'5, 260 pounds, he brings excellent size and blocking ability, but there's also some red zone upside here. Roush will be the No. 2 TE on the Bears, eventually. His Day 2 draft capital means the Bears will likely stick to primarily 12 personnel moving forward.

players.name: Nate Boerkircher
players.analysis: Boerkircher is one of the best blocking TEs in the draft, but he boasts an excellent catch radius and range in the red zone. After spending four years as a back-up at Nebraska, he became the top TE for Texas A&M in 2025. Despite only having 19 catches, he did score 3 TDs. Boerkircher's Round 2 draft capital was surprising, but he does everything pretty well (and nothing great). He likely sticks as the Jaguars No. 2 TE, even if Brenton Strange enters free agency after this season.

players.name: Isiah Pacheco
players.analysis: A broken right fibula ruined Pacheco's 2024. Even when he returned late in the year, he split work with veteran Kareem Hunt. Pacheco failed to rebound last season but landed in a nice handcuff spot in Detroit.

players.name: Jarquez Hunter
players.analysis: Hunter made a name for himself dominating Alabama as a sophomore, but saved his best season for his senior year in '24. With 1,201 yards rushing and another 155 through the air, he is an intriguing two-way player with a strong lower body to work in traffic. However, he didn't see the field in 2025, as Kyren Williams and Blake Corum handled almost all of the backfield work. That duo remains under contract for 2026.

players.name: Isaiah Davis
players.analysis: Davis' college tape featured a nice combo of power, patience, and vision. The Jets' landing spot just hasn't been a friendly one, especially with Breece Hall returning on the franchise tag. Davis will also be pushed by third-year RB Braelon Allen.

players.name: Kirk Cousins
players.analysis: Cousins returned to the starting lineup following Michael Penix's ACL tear last season. The results were mixed, though, and Cousins will play in Vegas in 2026. He's expected to open 2026 as the starter while the team brings along top pick Fernando Mendoza.

players.name: Darnell Washington
players.analysis: Despite playing with Pat Freiermuth and Jonnu Smith, Washington emerged as a versatile weapon with his size and after-catch ability. Washington later broke his arm and ended up on IR, but he'll return in 2026 and could earn more work for new HC Mike McCarthy.

players.name: Tua Tagovailoa
players.analysis: Tua was benched late in the 2025 season, extending a downward trend that began in 2024. Landing with the Falcons allows him a shot at making 2026 starts, especially with Michael Penix Jr. rehabbing an ACL tear. Still, we're unenthusiastic about Tua's dynasty outlook.

players.name: Tyler Higbee
players.analysis: Higbee signed a new two-year deal with the Rams in March. A crowded TE depth chart continues to make him an unlikely fantasy factor.

players.name: Dont'e Thornton Jr.
players.analysis: Thornton had plenty of preseason hype, but that didn't come to fruition in his rookie year. Thornton went 10-135-0 during the 2025 season despite often playing an outside role early in the season. Perhaps a new coaching staff can maximize Thornton's size and speed.

players.name: Andrei Iosivas
players.analysis: Iosivas continues working as the No. 3 WR for the Bengals behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. He saw a boost when one of those players were out and can be useful in deeper leagues. Iosivas' athleticism should allow him to stick in the league for awhile.

players.name: Trevor Etienne
players.analysis: Etienne showed pro potential at Florida, but he played behind a true freshman after transferring to Georgia. Like his brother Travis, Trevor has pass-catching ability that could eventually be utilized in the pros. However, he may be more of a third-down back than a starter. His rookie year turned up only 23 touches behind Rico Dowdle and Chuba Hubbard.

players.name: Raheim Sanders
players.analysis: Rocket Sanders looked like a future NFL stud after his sophomore season at Arkansas, rushing for 1,443 yards. But he dealt with multiple injuries and settled in for a mediocre year at South Carolina in 2024. Being nearly 230 pounds with insane explosion off the snap, he does boast some enticing traits. There's just not a clear path to him becoming a valuable fantasy asset.

players.name: Darren Waller
players.analysis: Waller returned from retirement in 2025 and offered the Dolphins a red zone target. Turning 34 early next season, there's a chance he heads back to retirement.

players.name: Brashard Smith
players.analysis: Similar to Tyrone Tracy, Brashard Smith spent most of his collegiate career as a WR. After transferring to SMU from Miami, Smith changed positions to RB and was the central part of their offensive success. Lining up both wide and in the backfield, he is an intriguing weapon with great short-area quickness and ability. We saw flashes of that in Year 1, although the Chiefs appeared hesitant to truly unleash him. Smith will remain no more than a part-timer moving forward, especially after the signing of Kenneth Walker.

players.name: Tyquan Thornton
players.analysis: Thornton found a career resurgence with 19-438-3 on 37 targets, benefiting from injuries to the Chiefs' WR corps. He returned on a one-year deal this offseason and should continue in a downfield/rotational role.

players.name: Tanner Koziol
players.analysis: Koziol went 94-839-8 in 2024 with Ball State before transferring to Houston. His 74-727-6 showcases Koziol's pass-catching prowess. His massive wingspan makes him a mismatch at 6'7, 250 pounds. Koziol fell to Day 3 of the NFL Draft, but he offers more receiving upside than Nate Boerkircher (who was drafted ahead of him). It may be worth betting on Koziol to become the pass catcher if Brenton Strange becomes a free agent after this season.

players.name: Josh Cuevas
players.analysis: Cuevas found his largest role on Alabama's offense in 2025, going for 37-411-4. He figures to be a primary blocking TE at 256 pounds, but Cuevas does offer some red zone upside with his contested catching ability. Cuevas flashed a bit of receiving upside, but he will have to compete with fellow rookie Matthew Hibner for playing time behind Mark Andrews.

players.name: Ja'Tavion Sanders
players.analysis: Sanders ended as TE47 in PPR points per game in 2025, a disappointing season. A poor Panthers' passing game hurt Sanders' output, but at only 23, there's still a chance of him developing into a useful fantasy piece. Carolina remains thin at TE ahead of the NFL Draft.

players.name: Reggie Virgil
players.analysis: Virgil transferred from Miami (OH) to Texas Tech, showcasing his speed as a threat next to WR Caleb Douglas. Virgil is 6'3 with a big wingspan and offered a downfield contested catch option. Virgil went early in Round 5 and could crack the Cardinals depth chart down the line as a No. 4 WR.

players.name: Matthew Hibner
players.analysis: Hibner's size and quick feet make him a great blocking TE and a reliable red zone option. He went 31-436-4 at SMU last year and worked more downfield as the season went on. Hibner could make the Ravens' roster as their No. 2 TE, but he will mostly be an in-line blocker.

players.name: Kaytron Allen
players.analysis: Allen has four straight seasons of over 860 rushing yards. He has been the consistent backfield presence and ascended past teammate Nicholas Singleton despite a difference in athleticism. Allen is one of the most technically sound RBs in the class, and that shows with him averaging over 5 yards per carry in every college season. He wasn't drafted until the sixth round, but Allen lands in a weak Commanders' RB depth chart.

players.name: Noah Fant
players.analysis: In 2025, Fant flashed a bit but played behind Mike Gesicki when Gesicki was healthy. Then in March, he signed a two-year deal with New Orleans, where he'll compete for snaps alongside Juwan Johnson.

players.name: Arian Smith
players.analysis: Smith had good draft capital, but he could barely crack the lineup. He played behind Adonai Mitchell and John Metchie. That doesn't bode well for Smith's future.

players.name: Cole Kmet
players.analysis: Kmet started strong in 2025, but he fell behind rookie Colston Loveland by the end of the season. Even with D.J. Moore in Buffalo, Kmet's targets figure to remain limited going forward.

players.name: Daniel Bellinger
players.analysis: Bellinger posted a quiet 19-286-2 line in 2025. But he signed a notable three-year deal worth $14 million guaranteed in March, reuniting him with his former HC, Brian Daboll. Bellinger will push second-year TE Gunnar Helm for playing time.

players.name: Xavier Hutchinson
players.analysis: Hutchinson had a decent snap share despite the Texans drafting two rookies. But, he clearly isn't talented enough to be a consistent fantasy presence. He likely will be on the roster bubble in 2026.

players.name: Tai Felton
players.analysis: Felton was mostly pegged as a special teams and developmental player for the Vikings. He didn't make much impact as a rookie, but should stick on the roster for the future and could have some upside.

players.name: Jalon Daniels
players.analysis: Daniels held his own during a brief starting stint in place of Baker Mayfield. He likely tops out as a career backup, but his rushing ability adds some fantasy appeal if he gets another opportunity to start.

players.name: Mitchell Evans
players.analysis: Evans had a few shining moments in 2025. However, the lack of a passing game for the Panthers and a TE room full of second-tier options doesn't give Evans much space to emerge.

players.name: Rasheen Ali
players.analysis: The Ravens used a 2024 Round 5 pick on Ali, who posted two years of major production at Marshall. He'll continue pushing for scraps left behind by Derrick Henry.

players.name: Will Kacmarek
players.analysis: Kacmarek played second fiddle to Max Klare at Ohio State, but he was just as reliable a target. A blocker first with long arms at 6'6, Kacmarek does have soft hands and is dependable underneath. Kacmarek got Day 2 draft capital, but he will be exclusively a blocking TE. The playing time may be good, but he won't put up consistent fantasy numbers.

players.name: Justin Joly
players.analysis: Joly has been a consistent producer, with three straight seasons over 480 yards receiving. He continued thriving after transferring up from UConn to NC State. Joly fell to Day 3, but he has the ability to play HC Sean Payton's "Joker" role on the team after Evan Engram leaves. He has intriguing receiving upside.

players.name: Kaden Wetjen
players.analysis: Wetjen is one of the top returners in the draft, but that may translate into draft capital and snaps (as we saw with Chimere Dike last year). He was fifth on Iowa in receiving yards last year (151). He will be a return only player on the Steelers.

players.name: Jake Tonges
players.analysis: Tonges found success when George Kittle was injured, but there's no value here when the veteran is healthy.

players.name: Luke Musgrave
players.analysis: Musgrave hasn't emerged as a legit fantasy threat, even after Tucker Kraft's ACL tear last season. Musgrave will return to compete for a backup role in 2026.

players.name: Garrett Nussmeier
players.analysis: Nussmeier fell to Round 7 of the 2026 draft, landing with the Chiefs at No. 249 overall. He gets an ideal developmental setup under HC Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes, but his draft capital makes an eventual starting role a long shot. The LSU product is most likely to settle in as a career backup.

players.name: Dawson Knox
players.analysis: Knox overachieved in 2025, given Dalton Kincaid's injury struggles. The result: 36 catches, 417 yards, and 4 TDs, giving him his best fantasy output since 2022. He can be usable when Kincaid is on the sideline, but Knox won't be a consistent fantasy presence. In March, he agreed to a revised contract to remain with the Bills.

players.name: Tyler Goodson
players.analysis: Goodson emerged as Dallas' No. 2 RB early in the 2026 season, but he's unlikely to stick in that role long-term.

players.name: Devontez Walker
players.analysis: Walker has become a special-teams player for the Ravens, mixing in the occasional route. If they address WR at all, Walker may be further down the depth chart in 2026.

players.name: DJ Giddens
players.analysis: Giddens had two straight 1,000-yard rushing seasons for Kansas State (2023-2024), showing power and quickness as the lead back. He may not quite have the full range of NFL athleticism, but Giddens could eventually develop into a role player. He managed only 26 carries (3.7 YPC) as a rookie.

players.name: Jonnu Smith
players.analysis: Smith endured a disappointing season after being traded to the Steelers. He ended as TE45 in PPR points per game and was more effective running the ball than catching. He hits free agency ahead of his age-31 season.

players.name: Lewis Bond
players.analysis: Bond has led Boston College in receiving every season since Zay Flowers left for the NFL. He also had 30+ more receptions every season than the player who ranked second on the team. Bond is a bit thin, but he is shifty and has after-the-catch ability. Bond will likely play special teams for the Texans, but may develop into a WR who gets some snaps.

players.name: Dallen Bentley
players.analysis: Bentley earned the starting job at Utah, going 48-620-6 this past season. A solid blocker with soft hands, he lacks starting TE upside but could contribute as a No. 2 TE. He will be a blocking reserve at best for the Broncos.

players.name: Ty Johnson
players.analysis: Johnson enjoyed a solid 2024 with a career-high 3 receiving TDs. He remained a part-timer behind James Cook in 2025 and enters '26 with one year left on his contract.

players.name: Ben Sinnott
players.analysis: Sinnott got an opportunity when Zach Ertz went down with an injury in 2025, but he wasn't able to do much with the playing time. Sinnott enters the key third year, but there is no indication that he will carry a sizable role. That's especially true after Washington added Chig Okonkwo on a free agent deal.

players.name: Samaje Perine
players.analysis: Perine returned to the Bengals in 2025 and saw his highest carry total (84) since 2022. He'll play next season at 31 and will remain no more than a handcuff.

players.name: KaVontae Turpin
players.analysis: Turpin makes his money on special teams, but the Cowboys have used him here and there for gadget plays/designed touches. Barring injuries ahead of him, there's no fantasy value outside of the return game.

players.name: Jack Endries
players.analysis: Endries transferred from Cal to Texas to replace Gunnar Helm and had a connection with QB Arch Manning. He went 33-346-3. He is a good route runner who can play in-line or in the slot. Endries will have a battle to even make the Bengals roster, but his intriguing receiving upside makes him a stash in very deep dynasty leagues.

players.name: Tommy Tremble
players.analysis: Tremble re-signed with the Panthers in 2025, but he posted another quiet season in the fall (27-249-2). There's not much fantasy value to chase here.

players.name: Jacob Cowing
players.analysis: Cowing wasn't able to make an impact in 2025, landing on IR with a hamstring injury.

players.name: Joe Royer
players.analysis: Royer transferred from Ohio State to Cincinnati. He went 29-416-4 with QB Brendan Sorsby, a potential Round 1 pick in 2027. A soft hands in-line TE at 6'5, 250 pounds, Royer will make his NFL bones as a blocker. He could be the occasional end zone target as well, but don't expect huge fantasy numbers. He should settle as the No. 2 TE next to Harold Fannin. That would make Royer mainly a blocker.

players.name: Kalif Raymond
players.analysis: Raymond popped for a couple of useful early-season fantasy lines, but his age and lackluster history of production make him a weak dynasty hold.

players.name: Jackson Hawes
players.analysis: Hawes is a blocking TE, but the Bills still utilized him at times in the red zone. He doesn't offer much upside as long as Dalton Kincaid is on the roster.

players.name: J. Michael Sturdivant
players.analysis: Sturdivant showed some early promise in college at Cal, but struggled to make a major impact at Florida in 2025. Sturdivant went undrafted and will have an uphill battle to make the Packers' roster.

players.name: Riley Nowakowski
players.analysis: Nowakowski was overshadowed by the WRs at Indiana, but he was a reliable target for Fernando Mendoza. His 32-387-2 season in 2025 showcased strong blocking and great stick routes against zone coverage. Nowakowski will profile as the third TE on the Steelers

players.name: Tutu Atwell
players.analysis: Atwell managed only 6 catches in 10 games for the Rams in 2025. He then signed a one-year deal with a Miami squad that's paper-thin at WR. Still, Atwell's career trajectory -- plus Miami's uncertainty at QB -- makes it hard to forecast a fantasy-friendly 2026.

players.name: Marcus Mariota
players.analysis: In 2025, Mariota supplied spot-start value as a fill-in for Jayden Daniels. The veteran notched three top-10 fantasy finishes, peaking at QB3. He signed a new deal to remain Jayden Daniels' backup in 2026.

players.name: Bauer Sharp
players.analysis: Sharp was a high school QB who transitioned to TE at SE Louisiana. He transferred up to Oklahoma, then LSU, as he improved at the position. Sharp is still raw, going for 24-252-2 this past season. Sharp will have to battle to make the Buccaneers' roster.

players.name: Isaac Guerendo
players.analysis: Guerendo brings excellent long speed, and he showed it at the Combine with a 4.33 forty-time. He also jumped 41.5 inches and tallied a 10’9” broad jump – all at 221 pounds. We saw that in a narrow window in 2024, although injuries limited his late-season impact. The 49ers showed their lack of faith in Guerendo by using a Round 5 pick on '25 rookie Jordan James. They also traded for Brian Robinson Jr. Ultimately, Guerendo is just a dynasty stash.

players.name: Luke McCaffrey
players.analysis: McCaffrey got some work in 2025 when injuries hit the Commanders' WRs, but a broken collarbone ended his season. McCaffrey should stick on the roster, but he will likely have to compete with incoming rookies/FAs for a contributing spot.

players.name: Jaren Kanak
players.analysis: Kanak only has one year of TE experience under his belt. He started his career as an LB before transitioning to TE in 2025. He went 44-533-0 despite the unfamiliarity with the position. Kanak will likely be a practice squad candidate for the Titans.

players.name: CJ Williams
players.analysis: Williams was a major reach by the Jaguars and enters a crowded WR depth chart. He went 59-749-6 at Stanford,  but doesn't showcase NFL athleticism.

players.name: Davis Allen
players.analysis: Allen posted a career-best 24-208-3 line in 2025. But with Terrance Ferguson on the ascent, Allen is unlikely to become a fantasy factor in L.A.

players.name: Emari Demercado
players.analysis: In 2025, Demercado posted nice efficiency numbers as a fill-in for injured RBs Trey Benson and James Conner. Still, Demercado projects as no better than the RB3 under new OC Mike LaFleur.

players.name: Jake Briningstool
players.analysis: Briningstool arrived as a 2025 UDFA, but a hamstring injury erased his rookie season. He'll return to compete for a depth role in 2026.

players.name: Demarcus Robinson
players.analysis: Robinson joined the 49ers in 2025 and played more toward the end of the season, given injuries in front of him. He'll retain a reserve role in 2026.

players.name: John Metchie
players.analysis: Metchie flashed in 2025 after injuries struck the Jets' WR corps. He finished at 33-274-2. He should stick with the Jets roster as a reserve and could be useful if injuries hit again.

players.name: Cade Stover
players.analysis: Stover appeared in only nine games this past season due to a broken foot. He suffered a partially torn MCL and PCL damage in the postseason but avoided surgery. He'll return as a depth piece behind Dalton Schultz.

players.name: Seydou Traore
players.analysis: Traore peaked in 2022 for Arkansas State going 50-655-4, but he was a reliable receiving option for Mississippi State the last two years. Traore will be an International Player Pathway player and not count against the Dolphins' roster. He will likely take time to develop.

players.name: Chip Trayanum
players.analysis: Trayanum has encountered a volatile college career. A four-star RB recruit at Arizona State, he flashed elite athleticism at 220 pounds as a freshman. He eventually moved to LB and transferred to Ohio State, where he would pivot back to RB. He went 182-1015-12 on the ground this past year, albeit with underwhelming advanced metrics. Trayanum's age and late breakout likely signal a later-round pick.

players.name: Kendrick Law
players.analysis: Law was a former top recruit for Alabama but broke out in 2025 at Kentucky (53-540-3). The Round 5 pick can play in the slot or outside and supplies good athleticism and soft hands. Unfortunately, a spring ACL tear will wipe out his entire rookie season and make him a dynasty longshot.

players.name: Jeremy Ruckert
players.analysis: Ruckert signed a new deal to stay with the Jets in December. He projects as the No. 2 TE behind second-year man Mason Taylor.

players.name: CJ Dippre
players.analysis: Dippre transferred out of Maryland ahead of the 2023 season. He chose Alabama over Ohio State in the transfer portal, although big-time production never followed (32 catches, 441 yards, and 0 TDs over the past two seasons). Dippre ultimately checks boxes for size and play strength, although he went undrafted in 2025. He was held without a catch as a rookie.

players.name: Riley Leonard
players.analysis: A developmental QB, Leonard saw some action in 2025 after injuries hit the QB room. He flashed with two rushing TDs and a surprising 270-2 passing line against Houston in Week 18. Still, we're likely looking at a long-term backup here.

players.name: DJ Rogers
players.analysis: Rogers showcased his athleticism last year for TCU. At 6'4, 250 pounds, he brings intriguing upside but never put everything together for consistent playing time. He went 34-319-2 in 2025. Rogers will likely be a late-round pick as a developmental receiving TE.

players.name: Luke Schoonmaker
players.analysis: Schoonmaker sits behind Jake Ferguson on the depth chart and doesn't have a path to playing time for the foreseeable future.

players.name: Jaydon Blue
players.analysis: Blue was expected to be the next big Texas RB after Sophomore CJ Baxter went down with an injury. However, struggles with his vision early in 2024 led to a pass-catching role for the former four-star recruit. Blue ran a 4.38 at the NFL Combine despite nursing a torn muscle in his groin. His 4.25 Pro Day time may be more accurate to his actual speed. As the first RB drafted by the Cowboys, Blue carried some appeal entering the '25 season. But he barely saw the field and watched as Javonte Williams rebounded in a major way. Dallas then re-signed Williams to a three-year contract, putting a lid on Blue's dynasty value.

players.name: Jeff Caldwell
players.analysis: Caldwell transferred to Cincinnati from Lindenwood and flashed incredible athleticism in 2025. He's 6'4, 210 pounds and will be a Combine stud both in the vertical and 40 time. He will have to battle to make the Chiefs after going undrafted.

players.name: Michael Trigg
players.analysis: Trigg was a highly recruited TE who started at USC. He transferred to Ole Miss and did very little before finally finding a good home at Baylor. His output: 50 catches, 694 yards, and 6 scores. Trigg's athleticism allows him to do damage after the catch at 6'4, 240 pounds. Trigg went undrafted due to character and effort concerns, but there is an opening to make the Cowboys' roster.

players.name: John Michael Gyllenborg
players.analysis: Gyllenborg flashed as a receiving weapon for Wyoming in 2024, going 30-425-3. He dealt with injuries in 2025, taking a step back, but Gyllenborg would be a receiving TE who could emerge with opportunity. He went undrafted, but the Chiefs are a good situation for Gyllenborg to make the roster.

players.name: Jimmy Horn Jr.
players.analysis: Horn played mostly on special teams, but he flashed a bit as a receiver. He could make the roster in 2026 and have a bigger impact, but should only be rostered in deep leagues.

players.name: RJ Maryland
players.analysis: Maryland is a receiving first TE who had consistent production over his four years at SMU. Though he won't test very well, Maryland could make a fantasy impact if he receives playing time. He went undrafted, but could make the Packers' team as the No. 3 TE.

players.name: Tip Reiman
players.analysis: Reiman dealt with injuries for most of last season and is stuck behind Trey McBride. Reiman has two years left on his rookie deal.

players.name: CJ Donaldson
players.analysis: Donaldson started his college career as a FB, but his between-the-tackles ability grew to a sizable role at West Virginia. He had two straight seasons with 730+ yards and 11 rushing TDs. The transfer to Ohio State didn't help much as he fell behind freshman RB Bo Jackson. Donaldson went undrafted.

players.name: Devin Culp
players.analysis: Culp caught a TD last season, but he played only 56 snaps as a rookie. There's not much of a ceiling here, especially after the Bucs re-signed Cade Otton.

players.name: Jaydn Ott
players.analysis: Ott burst onto the scene as a true freshman at Cal in 2022, going 170-897-8 on the ground and 46-321-3 through the air. He followed that up with 1,315 yards and 12 TDs rushing in 2023. Injuries cut his 2024 short, but Ott transferred to Oklahoma in hopes of hitting it big. He never climbed the depth chart, rushing for only 68 yards. Ott went undrafted.

players.name: Behren Morton
players.analysis: Morton spent five years in college at Texas Tech. He helped carry the offense to a playoff berth, but Morton is a bit of a one-trick pony. He has a strong arm and not much else. Morton will have an uphill battle to make an impact on the Patriots' roster.

players.name: Derius Davis
players.analysis: Davis is a special teamer who gets the occasional touch, but he will be unlikely to make a fantasy impact in 2026 and beyond.

players.name: Anthony Gould
players.analysis: Gould is still a special teams player with speed who makes little fantasy impact.

players.name: Donaven McCulley
players.analysis: McCulley dealt with injuries in 2024 and was pushed out of Indiana. He transferred to Michigan, where he tallied 39-588-3 on a run-first offense. He is a big X WR. McCulley went undrafted.
